sides.highlights: Looking back over Cortina and the Tofane, Cristallo and Sorapiss on either side at the top.

sides.character: From Misurina more a rolling link than a climb: briefly downhill, then gently back up to the top. As the way down towards Misurina it holds no difficulties.
sides.highlights: Shortly before Misurina, the view to the Cadini di Misurina.

campo-carlo-magno.intro: Named after the legend that Charlemagne crossed the Alps here. Madonna di Campiglio made cycling history in 1999, when Marco Pantani, having won the Giro stage, was excluded the next morning over a high haematocrit reading.

sides.character: Up out of the Val Rendena in steps, with flatter sections and finally through the resort of Madonna di Campiglio. The side of the Giro finishes, and the more varied one to climb.
sides.highlights: The Brenta group comes right up to the road in the upper part.

sides.character: From the Val di Sole at Dimaro through forest and a handful of hairpins, steepest low down and easing towards the top. An even road, good to ride in either direction.

passo-furcia.intro: The shortest way from the Pustertal into the Val Badia region: Olang on one side, St. Vigil in Enneberg on the other. An honest climb in the shadow of the Kronplatz, far less busy than the big Dolomite passes.

sides.character: From Olang through forest and a handful of hairpins, getting steeper towards the top. Little view on the way; at the top the meadows below the Kronplatz open up.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Kronplatz directly above the road.

passo-san-boldo.intro: A road you ride for the way it was built: hairpin after hairpin lies in tunnels in the rock, stacked one above the other in the wall above Tovena. Low, short and unique in the southern Alps.

sides.character: From Tovena unremarkable at first, then the wall with the hairpin tunnels, tight and controlled by lights, often with a short wait. Irregular, with short steep bits in the tunnels.
sides.highlights: The view from below of the stacked tunnel hairpins in the rock face.

passo-cibiana.intro: A quiet crossing between the Cadore and the Zoldo valley, hardly any traffic and plenty of forest. The village of Cibiana is known for the murals on its houses; above the pass, on Monte Rite, stands one of Reinhold Messner's mountain museums.

sides.character: Up from the Piave valley at Valle di Cadore in steps, with flatter sections and a short descent on the way, hairpins in the forest higher up. Long, but nowhere steep for long.
sides.highlights: The painted house fronts of Cibiana di Cadore along the way.

gampenjoch.intro: The link from Meran and Lana into the Nonsberg, a pass of length rather than hairpins. From the Adige it is one of the longest steady climbs in South Tyrol; from the south hardly more than a gentle rise.

sides.character: From Lana above the orchards steadily steep almost without a break, with only a few hairpins and a wide road. The side to ride up, because it is where the work is.
sides.highlights: Looking back over the Adige valley to Meran.

sides.character: From Fondo across the high ground of the Nonsberg, even and gentle. Downhill a calm roll-out, uphill more an approach than a climb.
sides.highlights: The German-speaking villages of Unsere Liebe Frau im Walde and St. Felix along the way.

passo-lavaze.intro: A pass of meadow rather than rock: at the top lies a wide plateau between Latemar and Schwarzhorn, cross-country skiing country in winter. The south side out of the Val di Fiemme is short and steep, the north side via Deutschnofen long and rolling.

sides.character: From Cavalese straight up the slope without hairpins, steep throughout and irregular, with sections well above the average. A test uphill, straight and fast downhill.
From Deutschnofen through meadows and forest in steps, with flat stretches and short descents on the way. Little gradient, plenty of landscape; the more pleasant side to descend.
sides.highlights: Latemar and Rosengarten in view above the meadows.

jochgrimm.intro: The short extension from the Lavazè pass up to just under 2,000 m, below the Schwarzhorn and the Weißhorn. More reward than climb: the view reaches far across the Adige valley and the Dolomites.

sides.character: From the junction on the Lavazè pass evenly and moderately steep across alpine pasture, almost without hairpins. An encore that costs hardly any effort.
sides.highlights: At the top the Schwarzhorn and Weißhorn directly above the road.

mendelpass.intro: Kaltern's home mountain: out of the vineyards and up the Mendel wall in hairpins, with the Adige valley and the Dolomites behind you. Alongside the road the Mendelbahn, one of the steepest funiculars in Europe, runs to the top.

sides.character: From Kaltern evenly up the wall in many tight hairpins, each ramp visible ahead. A fine rhythm uphill; downhill, with traffic, rather hard work.
sides.highlights: Looking back over the Kalterer See and the Adige valley to the Rosengarten.

sides.character: From the Nonsberg at Sarnonico short, with a flat step on the way, almost without hairpins. Not much as a climb, pleasant as the way down into the Nonsberg.

penegal.intro: From the Mendel Pass almost 400 m further up to the lookout tower on the Penegal. Short, steep and with one of the widest views over the Adige valley.

sides.character: From the Mendel Pass straight away steep through forest and a tight series of hairpins, easing a little towards the top. A short, hard second helping.
sides.highlights: From the tower, the view over the Adige valley to the Dolomites.

passo-brocon.intro: Between Valsugana and Primiero lies a pass without an audience: wide meadows, hardly any cars and the Pale di San Martino to the north. If you are after quiet rather than names, this is the place.

sides.character: From Castello Tesino long and in steps, with flatter sections and some hairpins in the upper part. Rarely steep, much forest and open meadows.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Pale di San Martino to the north.

passo-cereda.intro: A short crossing beneath the south faces of the Pale di San Martino, between Primiero and Agordo. Usually ridden as a link between bigger passes; the west side is short and full of hairpins, the east side long and gentle.

sides.character: Up from Fiera di Primiero in many hairpins, getting steeper towards the top. Compact and easy to pace, the rewarding side to climb.
sides.highlights: The south faces of the Pale above the Primiero.

sides.character: From Agordo long and in steps, with an intermediate saddle and a descent on the way, mostly gentle. Downhill a long, calm roll-out towards the Cordevole.

cima-grappa.intro: A lone mountain above the Venetian plain, with more than 1,500 m of climbing in one go from every side. In the 2014 Giro d'Italia an uphill time trial finished here, won by Nairo Quintana; at the top the First World War ossuary and the view to the Adriatic.

sides.character: From Semonzo narrow and irregular through a long series of hairpins, shadeless in the upper part. The rougher, steeper ascent, more impressive uphill than down.
From Possagno long and in steps, with a short descent on the way and a few steep ramps in between. Varied, but without a clear preferred direction.
sides.highlights: At the start in Possagno, the temple of the sculptor Antonio Canova.

sides.character: From Romano d'Ezzelino the wider main road, long even hairpins and steeper towards the top. Easy to read, and the most pleasant of the three sides to descend.
sides.highlights: With every hairpin the view across the plain towards the lagoon widens.

strada-della-forra.intro: The road out of the Brasa gorge from Lake Garda up to Tremosine, hewn into overhanging rock and through dark tunnels. Known too from the car chase at the start of the James Bond film "Quantum of Solace".

sides.character: From the lakeshore into the narrow gorge, beneath rock overhangs and through tunnels, then up in steps onto the plateau. The gradient is secondary; the narrowness and the traffic are not.
sides.highlights: The rock overhangs of the gorge; at the top the view from Tremosine over Lake Garda.

seiser-alm.intro: Europe's largest high alpine pasture, with the Schlern and the Langkofel as a backdrop. Because the road is closed to cars during the day it belongs to cyclists and the service bus, one of the rare Dolomite climbs without sightseeing traffic.

sides.character: From Seis steadily and fairly steeply up through forest and hairpins, until the pasture opens out at Compatsch. At the top the alpine roads are worth riding on.
sides.highlights: At Compatsch the view across the pasture to the Langkofel and Plattkofel.

rittner-hochplateau.intro: The sun terrace above Bozen: first the hairpins out of the Adige valley, then almost level roads across meadows and larches, with the Rosengarten and the Schlern opposite. On top runs the Rittner Bahn, and near Lengmoos stand the earth pyramids.

sides.character: From Bozen first steeply out of the basin in hairpins, then in steps and finally almost level across the plateau towards Lengstein. Work below, a scenic cruise on top.
sides.highlights: The earth pyramids near Lengmoos and the view to the Rosengarten and Schlern.

altopiano-di-asiago.intro: The plateau of the Seven Communes, wide and almost flat on top, with positions and memorials of the mountain war everywhere along its edges. The ascent is long; the real goal is the loops across the plateau.

sides.character: From Bassano long and flat to the foot of the plateau, then up its edge in steps and hairpins. A lot of distance for the height, nowhere steep for long.
sides.highlights: Above Asiago, the war memorial on the Leiten hill.

altopiano-del-cansiglio.intro: The beech forest of the Cansiglio once supplied the Venetian Republic with timber for its fleet. Today the karst plateau is a quiet place of wide meadows and dense forest, above the plain and yet away from everything.

sides.character: From Vittorio Veneto long and in steps, with a marked descent on the way and some hairpins at the edge of the plateau. Dense beech forest at the top and almost no traffic.
sides.highlights: The open meadow basin of the Pian Cansiglio in the middle of the forest.

monte-pizzoc.intro: A short detour off the Cansiglio to the summit of Monte Pizzoc, on the southern edge of the plateau. At the top the view opens across the Venetian plain, on clear days as far as the lagoon.

sides.character: From the junction on the Cansiglio moderate at first, then increasingly steep to the summit. Short and easy to take in.
sides.highlights: From the summit, the view over the Venetian plain.

val-di-genova.intro: The waterfall valley on the edge of the Adamello, from the Val Rendena up beneath the glaciers at the Malga Bedole. Right at the entrance the Nardis falls tumble down; higher up the road is closed to cars by day in summer.

sides.character: Up the valley from Carisolo in steps, flat stretches alternating with short steep rises beside the stream. The further in, the narrower the road and the closer the glaciers.
sides.highlights: The Nardis falls at the entrance to the valley.

ultental-weissbrunn.intro: A dead-end valley behind Lana, past reservoirs to the Weißbrunnsee beneath the Weißbrunnspitze. Little gradient, little traffic, old farmsteads and, at St. Gertraud, the ancient Ultental larches: the counterpart to the Dolomite passes.

sides.character: Up the valley from St. Walburg along the Zoggler reservoir, flat with a few steep steps, the last one before the Weißbrunnsee. Quiet, a ride without hurry.
sides.highlights: The ancient larches near St. Gertraud.

martelltal.intro: From the Vinschgau up beneath the glaciers of the Cevedale: a dead end with 1,400 m of climbing. In 2013 a Giro stage was due to finish here and was cancelled for snow; otherwise the valley is known for its strawberries.

sides.character: From Goldrain a long moderate run into the valley with flat steps, then hairpins up to the Zufrittsee and a steep final section to the Enzianhütte. The climb gets harder towards the end.
sides.highlights: The Zufrittsee and, at the top, the north faces of the Cevedale.

schnalstal-kurzras.intro: From Naturns up to 2,000 m at the glacier, the whole valley a single dead end. Along the way lie the charterhouse of Karthaus and the Vernagt reservoir; the Iceman was found above the head of the valley in 1991.

sides.character: From Naturns steep at first through the narrow gorge, then irregular, flat stretches and fresh ramps all the way to Kurzras. Long, and the end drags.
sides.highlights: The Vernagt reservoir with the 3,000 m peaks behind it.

vorderkaser-pfossental.intro: A side valley of the Schnalstal, reached by a narrow, steep road up to the Vorderkaser inn. Barely known and barely used, but one of the steepest ramps around.

sides.character: From the junction in the Schnalstal steep and steeper still towards the top, with few hairpins and hardly any respite. Short, but only comfortable with a small gear.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Vorderkaser inn for a stop.

villnoesstal.intro: The valley beneath the Geisler peaks, Reinhold Messner's home and the subject of countless photos of the church of St. Johann in Ranui against the wall. Quiet, because it leads nowhere, with the Zanser Alm as the goal.

sides.character: From Klausen steep at first out of the Eisack valley, then in steps up the valley, noticeably steeper again from St. Magdalena to the Zanser Alm. The Geisler stay in front of your wheel the whole way.
sides.highlights: The church of St. Johann in Ranui in front of the Geisler peaks.

hochtannbergpass.intro: The crossing from the Bregenzerwald into the Lechtal, between Widderstein and Braunarlspitze. Short but high and open, with galleries against the avalanches on the slopes above.

sides.character: From Schröcken steadily steep through a few hairpins and galleries, a compact climb with views back into the valley. The side with character to ride up.
sides.highlights: The Widderstein above the top of the pass.

sides.character: From Warth short and gentle, only a little steeper towards the top, no hairpins across open meadows. Downhill a calm finish towards the Lechtal.

furkajoch.intro: A narrow mountain road between the Laternsertal and Damüls, little used and with an open grassy crest at the top. The view reaches to the Rätikon and the Arlberg; the west side is tight and unprotected in places.

sides.character: From Damüls short and in steps across alpine meadows, with two hairpins. The easy side, usually ridden straight after the Faschinajoch.
sides.highlights: At the top, the view to the Rätikon and the Arlberg.

faschinajoch.intro: A short crossing from the Großes Walsertal to Damüls, usually ridden as the prelude to the Furkajoch. Small, but steeper from Fontanella than its height suggests.

sides.character: From Fontanella short and steep with a few hairpins, a little steeper still towards the top. The real ascent.
sides.highlights: Looking back over the Großes Walsertal.

sides.character: From Damüls a rolling link with a short descent, hardly any height. Downhill, the brief run over to Damüls.

staller-sattel.intro: High above the Antholzer See the road leads from the Pustertal into the Defereggental, one of the quietest over 2,000 m. The southern ramp is single-track and opened to one direction at a time, which spares it most of the cars.

sides.character: From Antholz Mittertal past the lake, then single-track up the wall in hairpins, steeper towards the top. Uphill, with the lake below, the finer direction.
sides.highlights: The Antholzer See below the hairpins.

sides.character: From the Defereggental at Erlsbach first with a steep ramp, then more evenly across pastures to the top. Wider than the south side and more open as a descent.
sides.highlights: At the saddle, the small Obersee.

ploeckenpass.intro: The Romans already crossed here from Carinthia to Carnia. In the First World War the front ran across the top of the pass; today an open-air museum of positions and trenches recalls it.

sides.character: From Kötschach-Mauthen through the Valentin valley in steps, with a short descent on the way and the hairpins in the upper part. Moderately steep and even enough to flow well downhill.
From Paluzza via Timau long and moderate, then markedly steeper with many hairpins in the final kilometres. The side to climb, with its climax at the end.
sides.highlights: At the top, the positions of the open-air museum at the pass.

nassfeldpass.intro: A ski resort on the border between Carinthia and Friuli, with a northern ramp counted among the hardest in Austria. From the south the road winds up out of the Val Canale in long series of hairpins.

sides.character: From Tröpolach out of the Gail valley hard and without a break, through many hairpins and if anything steeper towards the top. The side you set out to climb.
From Pontebba evenly through a long series of hairpins, hardly any outliers in the gradient. Just as demanding but more predictable, and good in either direction.

wurzenpass.intro: A border crossing into Slovenia whose reputation comes from the gradient, not the scenery. The northern ramp is short and brutally steep in its final kilometres, and lorries use it too.

sides.character: From Riegersdorf straight into long, straight steep sections, hardly any hairpins to catch your breath. A trial of strength uphill, unpleasant downhill because of the gradient and the traffic.
From Kranjska Gora moderately through forest, steeper only towards the border. The easy side, and the better choice as the descent into Slovenia.

loiblpass.intro: Traffic takes the tunnel that prisoners of the Loibl concentration camp sub-camp were forced to build; the old road over the top stays quiet and steep. The border between Carinthia and Slovenia runs across the top.

sides.character: From Ferlach a long way up the Loibl valley, in steps with a descent on the way, then a few very steep ramps on the old pass road at the top. A long run-up to a hard finish.
sides.highlights: The memorial to the concentration camp sub-camp at the northern tunnel portal.

sides.character: From Tržič increasingly steep, on the old road at the top through hairpins and steep ramps. Shorter than the north side, similarly hard at the finish.

seebergsattel.intro: A quiet border crossing between the Karawanks and the Kamnik Alps, east of the Loibl. Even, little used and more meadow than rock at the top, with the faces of Kočna and Grintovec above Jezersko.

sides.character: From Zgornje Jezersko moderate at first, then a little steeper through a few hairpins to the border. A short, quiet climb without surprises.
sides.highlights: Looking back to the Kamnik Alps above Jezersko.

kesselberg.intro: The hairpin road between the Kochelsee and the Walchensee was long the scene of hill climb races and is still a magnet for motorcyclists, correspondingly loud on fine weekends. Short, but the view of the Walchensee carries it.

sides.character: From Kochel flat along the lake at first, then up the Kesselberg in a tight series of hairpins, getting steeper towards the top. Short and twisty, most pleasant on weekdays.
sides.highlights: The Walchensee power station at the start, the view of the Walchensee at the top.

sudelfeld.intro: From the Leitzach valley across the ski slopes of the Sudelfeld over into the Inn valley. The short west side from Bayrischzell is steep; the long east side passes the Tatzelwurm waterfall.

sides.character: From Bayrischzell short and steep, getting steeper towards the top, almost without hairpins. Quickly done uphill, straight and fast downhill.
From Oberaudorf long and in steps through forest past the Tatzelwurm, with flatter sections in between. As the descent into the Inn valley, the calmer, longer choice.
sides.highlights: The Tatzelwurm waterfall along the way.

riedbergpass.intro: Germany's highest pass road and one of its steepest too. It links the Iller valley at Obermaiselstein with Balderschwang and in summer is a short, hard test in the Allgäu.

sides.character: From Obermaiselstein straight up the slope without hairpins, irregular with steep sections in the upper part. Short, but hardly any chance to recover.
sides.highlights: At the top, the view across the Allgäu Alps.

oberjoch.intro: With its 106 bends, the Jochstraße from Bad Hindelang is considered Germany's twistiest road. It is the main link into the Tannheimer Tal and correspondingly busy, but pleasantly even for cyclists.

sides.character: From Bad Hindelang straight into the bends of the Jochstraße, steepest low down, then flatter up to Oberjoch. Moderate, but rarely alone on the road.
sides.highlights: Looking back into the Ostrach valley.

sella-nevea.intro: A quiet saddle between the Kanin and the Montasch, framed by high limestone walls. The road leaves the Predil route at the Raibler See and practically ends in the ski resort; there is hardly any traffic.

sides.character: A long, gentle approach from Tarvisio via Cave del Predil, first past the lake, then up in steps with a few short steeper pitches between the rock walls.
sides.highlights: The Raibler See on the way, the walls of the Kanin and the Montasch at the top.

predilpass.intro: The old border crossing between the Val Canale and the Soča valley, usually ridden as the opener to the Vršič. Two very different sides: gentle past the Raibler See in the north, steep down the Koritnica valley to Bovec in the south.

sides.character: Flat from Tarvisio to Cave del Predil, then along the lake and up in steps to the summit. Easy-going uphill, quick and open as a descent.
sides.highlights: The Raibler See just below the summit.

sides.character: Out of the Soča valley through the narrow Koritnica valley, irregular with short very steep ramps. Better climbed than descended, where the steep straights demand hard braking.
sides.highlights: The Kluže fortress above the Koritnica gorge.

kaunertaler-gletscherstrasse.intro: One of the highest roads in Austria: from the Kaunertal past the Gepatsch reservoir up into the glacier world of the Ötztal Alps. Toll-free for bikes, and for the legs one of the hardest climbs in the Eastern Alps.

sides.character: First a long way along the valley floor and the reservoir with flatter sections, then in the upper part a dense run of hairpins above the tree line in thin air.
sides.highlights: The Gepatsch reservoir, and the glaciers in view at the top.

loser-panoramastrasse.intro: The toll road up the Loser is short but one of the steepest climbs in the Salzkammergut. The Altausseer See lies below, the plateau on the edge of the Totes Gebirge above, with the view across the Ausseerland.

sides.character: Steep from Altaussee right away, hairpins up the slope, steeper still towards the top. Hardly a breather, but more of the lake with every metre.
sides.highlights: The Altausseer See far below, the Totes Gebirge at the top.

postalm.intro: One of the largest alpine pastures in Austria, reached by a toll road from the Wolfgangsee. Not a summit in the strict sense but a wide, treeless plateau you roll across almost level before dropping into the Lammertal.

sides.character: From Strobl up through forest in hairpins onto the plateau, then a long, almost level stretch across the pastures and finally down in hairpins into the Lammertal.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Wolfgangsee, the open pasture at the top.

sportgastein.intro: The Gasteiner Alpenstraße leads from Bad Gastein into the furthest corner of the Gastein valley, the Nassfeld beneath the three-thousanders of the Goldberg group. A dead end with no through traffic and traces of the old gold mining.

sides.character: From Bad Gastein via Böckstein into the narrowing valley, in steps with short steep ramps and flatter stretches between them, almost without hairpins.
sides.highlights: The wide valley head of the Nassfeld beneath the peaks.

hochkar.intro: The Hochkar Alpenstraße is a short, very steep toll road in the limestone Alps of Lower Austria. At the ski area on top the view reaches across the Ybbstal Alps to the Ötscher.

sides.character: Double-digit steep from Lassing right away and if anything harder towards the top, with few hairpins. A climb to grit your teeth through; going down means a lot of braking.
sides.highlights: At the top the view across the Ybbstal Alps to the Ötscher.

kals-lucknerhaus.intro: The Kalser Glocknerstraße runs up the Ködnitz valley to the Lucknerhaus, right beneath the Großglockner. From the end of the road the south side of Austria's highest mountain stands directly above the valley head.

sides.character: Evenly steep from Kals up the Ködnitz valley, with few hairpins and hardly a flatter spot. The Glockner draws ever closer as you go.
sides.highlights: At the Lucknerhaus the Großglockner straight ahead.

pitztal-mittelberg.intro: The Pitztal leads deep into the Ötztal Alps up to beneath the Wildspitze, the highest mountain in Tyrol. A long valley ride with little gradient that only ends at the glacier car park in Mittelberg.

sides.character: Up the valley from Jerzens: long flat stretches through the villages, short steps in between. More of a ride out than a climb, with the glaciers at the valley head ahead.
sides.highlights: The glaciers beneath the Wildspitze at the valley head.

col-de-la-forclaz-martigny.intro: The crossing from Martigny into the Trient valley and on to Chamonix, one of the main roads between the Valais and the Mont Blanc area. The Tour de France crossed it in 2016 on the way to Finhaut-Emosson.

sides.character: Out of the Rhône valley in many hairpins through the vineyards, then through forest, steeper if anything towards the top. Steady, hard work with a growing view back over the valley.
sides.highlights: The view back to Martigny and the bend of the Rhône.

col-des-montets.intro: A low barrier between the Chamonix valley and Vallorcine, right beneath the Aiguilles Rouges. Short and never hard, but with the Mont Blanc range at your back.

sides.character: A short, even pitch up from Argentière in a few hairpins, more a crossing than a climb. At the top the high valley opens beneath the Aiguilles Rouges.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Argentière glacier and the Mont Blanc range.

col-des-mosses.intro: The broad main road from the Rhône valley into the Pays-d'Enhaut, with a high moor at the top instead of a summit. A solid, unexcited crossing that combines well with the Pillon and the Croix.

sides.character: From Le Sépey the steeper ramps come first, then it eases towards the top and the road runs out into the open moorland.

col-du-pillon.intro: The short pass between Les Diablerets and Gsteig, with the Diablerets massif and its glacier above the road. The cable car to Glacier 3000 starts at the top.

sides.character: A short, evenly steep pitch from Les Diablerets with few hairpins, the rock walls of the Diablerets always in view.
sides.highlights: The valley station of the Glacier 3000 cable car at the top.

col-de-la-croix.intro: Narrow, steep and quiet: the mountain road from Villars to Les Diablerets that leaves the valley road behind and crosses the alpine pastures. At the top the view of the Grand Muveran.

sides.character: Up from Villars in steps, steep pitches alternating with short flatter ones, almost without hairpins. The higher you go, the more open the pastures.
sides.highlights: The pastures at the top with the view of the Muveran.

jaunpass.intro: The crossing from the Simmental into the Gruyère country, over the language border from German into French. A quiet, even pre-Alpine pass through forest and pasture.

sides.character: From Boltigen through forest and pasture, with a number of hairpins and getting a little steeper towards the top. A climb for riding a rhythm.

pragelpass.intro: A narrow, steep mountain road between the Muotatal and the Klöntal, closed to cars on Sundays and public holidays. The Klöntalersee lies on the east side as the reward.

sides.character: Long and stepped from Muotathal, steep ramps alternating with short recovery stretches. Narrow, few hairpins, plenty of forest and pasture.

glaubenbielen.intro: The panoramic road from Giswil up to Sörenberg, across wide alpine pastures beneath the Brienzer Rothorn. Long, steep and quiet in summer, a classic of Central Switzerland.

sides.character: Long and even up from the Sarnersee, a little steeper still towards the top. Forest below, open pastures above with a view back over the lake.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Sarnersee, the Brienzer Rothorn at the top.

glaubenberg.intro: The quiet neighbour of the Glaubenbielen, from Sarnen into the Entlebuch. Long ramps through forest, moorland at the top and hardly any traffic even in summer.

sides.character: From Sarnen the steep ramps through the forest come first; in the upper part it eases and the road runs out into the moorland.

ibergeregg.intro: The short crossing between Schwyz and the Sihltal, with the rock teeth of the Mythen as constant companions. Open all year and only a short climb from Oberiberg.

sides.character: A short stretch over pastures from Oberiberg, moderate at first and a little steeper towards the end, with only a few hairpins.
sides.highlights: The Mythen in view at the top.

schwaegalp.intro: The summit lies right beneath the north face of the Säntis, and that wall carries the whole climb. The Säntis cable car starts at the top, with the Appenzell hill country all around.

sides.character: Up from Urnäsch through rolling country in steps, flat stretches between short steeper ones. For the last few kilometres the Säntis stands above the road.
sides.highlights: The north face of the Säntis over the last few kilometres.

forcola-di-livigno.intro: The high border crossing between Livigno and the Bernina area, bare and open. Usually part of the big loop over the Bernina and the Foscagno.

sides.character: Long and flat out of Livigno along the high valley, then up in steps without hairpins over bare ground to the border. Never very steep, but high and exposed to wind.

passo-d-eira.intro: The smaller of the two passes between Livigno and the Valtellina, right before the Foscagno. Short, usually taken in passing and busy because of duty-free Livigno.

sides.character: Out of the Livigno valley floor, short and moderately steep, a little steeper towards the top, with a few hairpins and a view over the high valley.
sides.highlights: The view back over Livigno and its lake.

passo-del-vivione.intro: One of the quietest mountain roads in the Bergamasque Alps, narrow and largely without crash barriers. It links the Val di Scalve with the Val Camonica and belongs to the few who find it.

sides.character: Moderate from Schilpario at first, then steeper in many tight hairpins up past the tree line into open ground.

passo-del-maniva.intro: The Maniva lies between the Val Trompia and the Valle del Caffaro, with a ridge road joining at the top. Long climbs, very little traffic and on clear days a view as far as Lake Garda.

sides.character: From Bagolino in many hairpins through the forest, getting steeper towards the top. Long, steady work without a real break.
sides.highlights: At the top, on clear days, the view as far as Lake Garda.

madonna-del-ghisallo.intro: Not a high pass but a place of pilgrimage for cycling: since 1949 the Madonna del Ghisallo has been the patron saint of cyclists, and the cycling museum stands beside the chapel. The climb from Bellagio is a fixture of the Giro di Lombardia.

sides.character: Steep from Bellagio right away in hairpins above Lake Como, then a flatter stretch through Civenna and a last short rise to the chapel.
sides.highlights: The chapel with the champions' jerseys and bikes, the view over Lake Como.

muro-di-sormano.intro: The Wall of Sormano is one of the steepest ramps ever used in a professional race. It disappeared from the Giro di Lombardia after 1962 and has been back since 2012; the gradients are painted on the tarmac.

sides.character: The measured line follows the regular road from Sormano to the Colma, even and moderately steep. The Wall itself is a short, far steeper section beside it.
sides.highlights: At the Colma the view over the Vallassina.

passo-dell-aprica.intro: The main link between the Valtellina and the Val Camonica, and busy accordingly. In the Giro often the approach to the Mortirolo and the Gavia; in 1994 Marco Pantani won the stage over the Stelvio and the Mortirolo at Aprica.

sides.character: Up from the Valtellina at Tresenda in steps, steeper ramps between calmer stretches and the valley below. The more demanding side and the better one to climb.
sides.highlights: The view over the Valtellina and its vineyards.

sides.character: Long and flat from Edolo along the valley, only short steeper pitches. Rather tedious uphill, quick and open as a descent to Edolo.

col-du-sanetsch.intro: One of the longest climbs in Switzerland: from Sion over 1,700 m of climbing in one go up to the reservoir in a bare karst landscape. A dead end for bikes; the way down is the same road, or the cable car to Gsteig.

sides.character: From Sion first through vineyards and villages, then up in hairpins with a short dip on the way, and at the top through several tunnels onto the treeless plateau.
sides.highlights: The reservoir at the end, with the glaciers of the Diablerets massif above it.

sestriere.intro: A regular of the Giro and the Tour. In 1952 Fausto Coppi won here at one of the Tour's first summit finishes, and in 1992 Claudio Chiappucci arrived alone after a long breakaway. Plain as scenery, heavy with history.

sides.character: Even from Cesana on a wide road with few hairpins, without surprises. A climb that is easy to pace.

valsavarenche.intro: The middle one of the valleys of the Gran Paradiso, entirely within the national park. The road ends at Pont beneath the summit, where the paths to the huts begin; with luck you will see ibex on the way.

sides.character: Up the valley from Villeneuve: first in hairpins out of the Aosta valley, then long and even through forest and meadows to the head of the valley.
sides.highlights: At the valley head in Pont, the Gran Paradiso in view.

rhemes-notre-dame.intro: A detour at the entrance of the Valsavarenche into the Val di Rhêmes, the westernmost valley of the Gran Paradiso area. The road ends in Rhêmes-Notre-Dame before a wide valley head.

sides.character: From the junction near Introd up the valley in steps, steep ramps alternating with long flatter stretches through villages and meadows.

valgrisenche.intro: A dead end in the Aosta valley that leads past the Beauregard reservoir up to beneath the glaciers of the Grande Sassière. After the lake almost nothing follows, just quiet and rock.

sides.character: Up from Arvier in steps, steep ramps and calmer sections in turn, in the upper part along the flank high above the reservoir.
sides.highlights: The Beauregard reservoir with the glaciers above.

valle-maira.intro: The quietest of the Piedmontese valleys, away from mass tourism. At its end the rock tooth of the Rocca Provenzale rises above Chiappera; you ride here for the peace, not the gradient.

sides.character: Up the valley from Acceglio, even and moderately steep, with a few hairpins through larches and pastures to the valley head.
sides.highlights: The Rocca Provenzale above Chiappera.

colle-di-nava.intro: The old crossing from the Riviera into the Tanaro valley, open all year. The Giro crossed it as early as 1953, and Milan–Sanremo used it in 2020 instead of the Turchino. Lavender fields at the top at almost 1,000 m.

sides.character: Even from Pieve di Teco on a wide road with barely any hairpins. The side with the height gain and the better one to climb.
From Ormea via Ponte di Nava little more than a gentle rise through the upper Tanaro valley. Undemanding uphill, a flowing run-out downhill.

colle-san-bartolomeo.intro: A winter training climb for the pros living on the Riviera, between the Impero valley and the Arroscia valley. Olive groves, hardly any traffic and a small village at the top.

sides.character: From Chiusavecchia in hairpins through the olive groves, a little steeper towards the top. Downhill the hairpins flow well, with the valley towards the sea ahead.
sides.highlights: Downhill the view down the Impero valley towards the coast.

sides.character: From Pieve di Teco up the slope without hairpins, with a steep ramp towards the top. Better climbed than descending that steep straight.

passo-del-ginestro.intro: The quiet neighbour of the Colle San Bartolomeo, open all year. Up through olives and broom, a view of both valleys at the top, and on the far side down to Cesio in the Arroscia valley.

sides.character: Long and irregular from Chiusanico through olives and broom, with flat stretches, a short dip and the odd steep ramp. The calmer choice downhill.
From Cesio only a short but steep pitch throughout, without hairpins. Quickly pushed up, a steep straight going down.

colle-del-melogno.intro: The home climb of Finale Ligure: from the sea through the beech woods to just over 1,000 m. A 19th-century fort stands at the top; the Calizzano side is the shorter and quieter one.

sides.character: Long and even from Finalborgo, almost at sea level, first through the hinterland, then through beech forest. The classic ascent and the side to climb.
sides.highlights: The fort at the top, and the view of the sea from the slope.

sides.character: Shorter and even from Calizzano through forest, with a few hairpins. Little traffic, calm and open as a descent.

passo-del-faiallo.intro: From the sea at Genoa-Voltri past the Acquasanta sanctuary onto the crest of the Ligurian Alps. At the top the coast lies far below in the haze, the Po plain on the other side.

sides.character: From Voltri, practically at sea level, long and stepped, with steep ramps, flatter stretches and a short dip on the way. On the crest the view back to the sea.
sides.highlights: At the top the view over Genoa and its gulf.

passo-del-turchino.intro: Since its first edition in 1907, Milan–Sanremo has crossed the Apennines here and caught its first sight of the sea. A low, busy crossing with a short tunnel at the top – famous for the race, not for the road.

sides.character: From Voltri on the coast steadily and gently up the Leira valley, more main road than mountain road; a few wide bends, never a moment that hurts.
sides.highlights: The tunnel at the top and the view over the Riviera, which the pros see in the opposite direction in the race.

monte-beigua.intro: The highest summit of the Beigua massif, barely 15 km as the crow flies from the beach: from Varazze you climb from sea level to almost 1,300 m. Antennas and wind at the top, and a view that on clear days reaches from the sea to the Alps.

sides.character: Up from the sea via Alpicella, moderate at first, then ever steeper, with the hardest ramps in the upper part. With the sea at your back, the climb you come here for.
sides.highlights: The view back over the coast and the Gulf of Genoa.

sides.character: From Sassello in the hinterland, long and in steps across the upland, with some height given back on the way. Quiet and rarely steep, the pleasanter side for rolling down inland.

passo-teglia.intro: One of the highest tarmac crossings in the Sanremo hinterland, almost 1,400 m up, links the Argentina valley with Rezzo. From chestnut forest up to the open pasture on the ridge, with almost nobody in between.

sides.character: Straight up from Molini di Triora, evenly steep through chestnut forest, hairpin after hairpin. No flat bit to recover on, but a clear rhythm.
From Rezzo gently at first, then steadily steeper, with the hard parts higher up. The longer, more flowing side, good for descending towards Pieve di Teco.

colle-d-oggia.intro: A quiet crossing between the Argentina hinterland and Rezzo, almost car-free and rideable all year. Up from Carpasio and down to Rezzo makes a fine loop in the hinterland of the Riviera.

sides.character: From Carpasio short and evenly steep, a few hairpins and you are at the top. The climb of the loop.
Long and stepped down to Rezzo, with flatter stretches and a short counter-climb. The descent of the loop; as a climb, a long way with rests.

colle-langan.intro: The crossing between the two finest valleys of the Sanremo hinterland, the Nervia valley at Pigna and the Argentina valley at Molini di Triora. Monte Toraggio stands above the top, and the road to the Colle Melosa branches off at the pass.

sides.character: From Pigna long and lonely through forest, restrained at the bottom, steeper at the top. Few hairpins, plenty of quiet: the side for going up.
sides.highlights: Monte Toraggio straight ahead at the top.

sides.character: From Molini di Triora in many hairpins that grow steeper towards the top. Shorter than the Pigna side; going down, the tight bends need attention.

colle-melosa.intro: A detour off the Colle Langan up to the Rifugio Allavena at the Colle Melosa, a good 1,500 m above the sea. One of the highest tarmac roads in the Sanremo hinterland, with views of the Ligurian Alps.

sides.character: On uphill from the Langan pass, irregular with changing ramps and only a few hairpins, more open at the top with distant views.
sides.highlights: The refuge at the end of the road for a break.

monte-bignone.intro: Sanremo's home mountain and one of the longest ascents on the Riviera dei Fiori: from the harbour in one go to over 1,000 m. The tarmac ends just below the summit.

sides.character: From the sea through the villa districts, then up in hairpins via San Romolo; it steepens towards the top, with the hardest stretches last.
sides.highlights: San Romolo as a stop halfway up, and the view over Sanremo and the coast at the top.

cipressa.intro: Since 1982 the penultimate climb of Milan–Sanremo and often the place where the race breaks apart. A short hill through olive groves to the village above the coast, famous but not hard.

sides.character: Up from the Aurelia at San Lorenzo, with varying gradient and a few hairpins among the olives; hard at race pace, a quarter of an hour at your own.
sides.highlights: The village of Cipressa at the top with a view of the sea.

poggio-di-sanremo.intro: The last climb of Milan–Sanremo, where the race has been decided since 1960: a few kilometres between greenhouses, the village at the top, then the descent to the Via Roma. Low, gentle, and still one of the most famous hills in cycling.

sides.character: Gently up from the coast road at Bussana between greenhouses, with a few hairpins and a short steeper bit before the village. Anyone who wants to can sprint the crest as in the race.
sides.highlights: The village of Poggio at the top, the Via Roma waiting below.

colle-scravaion.intro: A crossing behind Albenga that is open all year, from the castle village of Castelvecchio di Rocca Barbena over to Bardineto. The loops from the Finale area over the Melogno return to the sea here.

sides.character: Evenly up from the south without hard parts, past the castle of Castelvecchio. Downhill, with the view down the valley towards the coast, the finer direction.
sides.highlights: The castle village of Castelvecchio di Rocca Barbena on its rock.

sides.character: From Bardineto barely a climb: a few gentle kilometres across the upland to the pass. The direction you ride when returning from the hinterland loops to the sea.

colle-san-bernardo-di-garessio.intro: The old link from Albenga into the Tanaro valley at Garessio, open all year. Riders heading from the Riviera to the loops around Ormea and the Colle di Nava cross here.

sides.character: From Erli on the Neva a long way through chestnut forest, in steps with flatter stretches between, only a few hairpins. Flowing enough to enjoy on the way down.
From Garessio short and evenly steep in a run of hairpins. The compact climb you would rather ride up than down.

monte-ceneri.intro: The low saddle between Sopraceneri and Sottoceneri in Ticino, the road link between Bellinzona, Locarno and Lugano. Less busy since the Ceneri base tunnel, but no quiet road.

sides.character: From Cadenazzo on the Magadino plain steadily up through forest, a few wide bends on a broad road. The actual climb of the crossing.
From Rivera little more than a ramp: short and gentle up to the pass. The direction in which the crossing from Lugano happens almost in passing.

alpe-di-neggia.intro: From Lake Maggiore on the Gambarogno shore a good 1,000 metres of climbing in hairpins through chestnut forest, with the lake ever further below. Beyond the pass lies Indemini, a Swiss village connected to the road network only via Italy.

sides.character: From Vira on the lake in a long sequence of hairpins through chestnut forest, with flatter stretches between the steep ones. The lake at your back makes it the side to climb; downhill, the many tight bends are work.
sides.highlights: The view across Lake Maggiore towards Locarno.

sides.character: From Indemini short and evenly steep up to the pass. Downhill, the quick way over to Indemini and on into Italy.
sides.highlights: The stone village of Indemini.

sighignola.intro: The Balcone d'Italia: the road ends at the Swiss border on a ledge a good 1,000 m above Lake Lugano. Lugano below, and on a clear day the four-thousanders of the Valais on the horizon.

sides.character: From Lanzo d'Intelvi short and quiet up a few hairpins, steepest at the bottom and easing towards the top.
sides.highlights: The viewing ledge above Lugano at the end of the road.

monte-bisbino.intro: The home climb of Como's cyclists: from Cernobbio on the lake through forest to the pilgrimage church on the summit. At the top the view reaches over the southern part of Lake Como to the Po plain.

sides.character: From Cernobbio evenly steep in a long chain of hairpins through forest, hardly any traffic. A climb for finding your rhythm.
sides.highlights: The church on the summit and the view over Lake Como.

monte-generoso-bellavista.intro: A quiet dead end up Monte Generoso above Lake Lugano, as far as the Bellavista station of the rack railway. The summit above is left to the train and the walkers.

sides.character: Steeply up from Rovio through forest, alternating ramps and flatter sections, with a stretch of downhill on the way. The lake stays at your back.
sides.highlights: The view of Lake Lugano at Bellavista.

valle-verzasca.intro: Beyond Gordola over the Contra dam, from which James Bond jumped in GoldenEye, then along the clear green water of the Verzasca to Sonogno. One of the finest valleys in Ticino, full of bathers in high summer.

sides.character: Up the valley from Gordola: first in hairpins to the dam and along the reservoir, then in steps beside the river, between stone villages and granite to the head of the valley.
sides.highlights: The double-arched stone bridge Ponte dei Salti at Lavertezzo.

val-bavona.intro: The uppermost Maggia valley: a narrow road between granite walls, rockfalls and waterfalls, through hamlets without mains electricity to San Carlo. Hardly any cars, a lot of stone and a valley unlike any other in Ticino.

sides.character: Up the valley from Cevio: gently in steps along the river, a few short steeper bits, almost flat in between. The rock walls close in ever further.
sides.highlights: The waterfall at Foroglio, with a grotto there for a break.

mottarone.intro: The viewpoint mountain between Lake Maggiore and Lake Orta, with both lakes at the top and the Valais Alps with Monte Rosa beyond. From Stresa a private toll road leads up; the climb from Armeno is a public road without a toll.

sides.character: From Armeno via Gignese, with changing gradient, steep ramps and short recoveries, open pasture at the top.
sides.highlights: At the top the view of two lakes and Monte Rosa.

passo-di-valcava.intro: One of the steepest climbs in northern Italy: from Torre de' Busi over 1,000 metres in one go, a wall of hairpins above the Val San Martino. The east side from the Valle Imagna is the tamed half.

sides.character: From Torre de' Busi hard from the start and steeper still towards the top, hairpin after hairpin without a rest. Up, a test; down, nothing but braking.
From the Valle Imagna steady and much tamer, through forest and meadows. The side to descend.

culmine-di-san-pietro.intro: The crossing from the Valsassina into the Val Taleggio, part of the Giro d'Italia more than once. Two short sides over a wooded saddle, joined into a quiet loop between Lecco and Bergamo.

sides.character: From Moggio short, steady low down and steeper above, with few hairpins through forest. The compact side, good for climbing.
From Vedeseta in the Val Taleggio steepest at the bottom, easing towards the top. The quieter side, and downhill the way into the Taleggio valley.

monte-san-primo.intro: The extension of the Ghisallo: from Bellagio past the chapel of the Madonna del Ghisallo and on via Magreglio to beneath Monte San Primo, the highest summit of the Larian Triangle. Views of Lake Como again and again on the way.

sides.character: From Bellagio up the Ghisallo road in hairpins, a flatter stretch after the chapel, then steeper again to the end of the tarmac. A long climb in stages.
sides.highlights: The Madonna del Ghisallo with its cycling museum.

selvino.intro: Bergamo's home climb: out of the Val Seriana in a famous run of hairpins up to the Selvino plateau. This is where the area learns to climb, and the continuation via Aviatico into the Val Serina makes a loop of it.

sides.character: From Nembro up the valley side in closely stacked hairpins, with changing ramps and the odd flatter stretch. The Val Seriana below you.
sides.highlights: The view back down the hairpins and the Val Seriana.

colle-gallo.intro: A low crossing between the Val Seriana and the Val Cavallina with a cyclists' chapel at the top: the sanctuary of the Madonna dei Ciclisti, Bergamo's counterpart to the Ghisallo. A training loop of the local pros.

sides.character: From Gaverina Terme short and punchy, in many hairpins and steepest at the top. The side for climbing.
From Cene in the Val Seriana long and stepped, with flat stretches and only a few hairpins. Downhill, a flowing ride into the valley.

piani-dei-resinelli.intro: From Ballabio above Lecco in hairpins beneath the rock walls of the Grigna, until the road ends on the Resinelli plateau. Steep, shady and with a view of Lecco and the lake.

sides.character: From Ballabio straight into a tight run of hairpins, hardest at the bottom, a little easier towards the top. Mostly in shade.
sides.highlights: The walls of the Grigna and the view of Lecco.

passo-di-agueglio.intro: From Lake Como at Varenna up via Perledo and Esino Lario and down into the Valsassina. The lake side, with its hairpins and the view of Bellagio, is one of the finest climbs on the eastern shore.

sides.character: From Varenna up the lake flank in many hairpins, with flatter stretches in the villages. The lake and Bellagio lie behind and below you; downhill the tight bends are rather work.
sides.highlights: The view from Perledo across the lake to Bellagio.

sides.character: From Parlasco in the Valsassina short and even. Downhill, the quick way into the valley.

bocca-del-creer.intro: The high road over Monte Baldo: from Brentonico onto the ridge and over the Bocca di Navene down to Lake Garda, some 1,500 m above the water. The descent to the lake counts as the finest on the whole of Lake Garda.

sides.character: From Brentonico via San Valentino onto the ridge, with varying gradient through forest and alpine pasture. The shorter, controlled way up.
From the lake at Navene steep and narrow up the flank, then on along the ridge to the Bocca del Creer. Going down you ride with Lake Garda ahead of you, which makes it the side to descend.
sides.highlights: Lake Garda straight below the Bocca di Navene.

punta-veleno.intro: The steepest climb on Lake Garda: from the shore at Brenzone up the flank of Monte Baldo, with ramps up to 20 %. At the top the road tips over towards Prada Alta.

sides.character: Steep from the lakeshore without a run-up and steeper still above, hardly any hairpins, the road heads straight up the slope. Bring your smallest gear.
sides.highlights: The view straight down onto Lake Garda.

passo-del-ballino.intro: The classic way from Lake Garda into the Trentino: from Riva via Tenno past the Lago di Tenno up onto the Fiavè plateau. Open all year and busy at weekends.

sides.character: From Riva steepest at the bottom in hairpins above the lake, calmer and gentler at the top. Downhill you ride towards Lake Garda, the finer direction.
sides.highlights: The turquoise Lago di Tenno and the village of Canale di Tenno.

sides.character: From Ponte Arche in the Giudicarie gently and in steps across the plateau, almost without hairpins. Up, the easy side.

passo-d-ampola.intro: Not a mountain but the end of the Ledro valley: from the Lago di Ledro almost flat to the pass, then down to Storo in the Chiese valley. The road up the Tremalzo branches off here.

sides.character: From Molina along Lake Ledro and up the valley, hardly any gradient and no hairpins. Downhill, a roll back to the lake.
sides.highlights: The pile-dwelling museum at Molina on the lakeshore.

sides.character: From Storo in the Chiese valley the actual climb: hairpins and steep stretches, with a short downhill on the way. Up, the side with bite.

passo-tremalzo.intro: A detour from the Val di Ledro to over 1,700 m, with the tarmac ending at the pass. Beyond it starts the famous gravel road with tunnels towards Lake Garda, a mountain-bike classic.

sides.character: From the junction in the Ledro valley evenly steep through forest and in many hairpins, more open at the top with views of the mountains around Lake Ledro.

passo-santa-barbara.intro: The crossing from Rovereto into the Val di Gresta above the northern end of Lake Garda, crossed by the Giro d'Italia in 2025. Two very different sides: long and stepped from the Adige valley, short and steep from Nago.

sides.character: From Rovereto a long way via Isera and in many hairpins, with rests and a stretch of downhill on the way. Flowing enough for the descent into the Adige valley.
From Nago via Ronzo, very steep at the bottom, easing towards the top. A climb you would rather ride up than down.
sides.highlights: The view back to Lake Garda above Nago.

passo-vezzena.intro: The way from Lake Caldonazzo onto the plateau of Lavarone and Asiago, via the hairpins of the old Menador road, the Kaiserjägerstraße. The north side is the climb, the south side from the Asiago plateau barely one.

sides.character: From Caldonazzo in hairpins up the rock face onto the plateau, then on in steps across meadows and forest to the pass, with short counter-climbs.
sides.highlights: The view of Lake Caldonazzo from the hairpins.

sides.character: From the Asiago plateau gently and in steps across open pasture, hardly any hairpins. Downhill a calm roll back onto the plateau.

pian-delle-fugazze.intro: The crossing from the Adige valley into the Val Leogra beneath the Pasubio, a front line in the First World War and already ridden by the Giro in 1934. Near the pass, the Pasubio ossuary stands on the Colle Bellavista.

sides.character: From Rovereto a long way through the Vallarsa, in steps with flat stretches and short counter-climbs, hairpins at the top. Downhill a long, quiet ride back to the Adige valley.
From Valli del Pasubio short and steep in hairpins, hardest at the top. The side for climbing.
sides.highlights: A detour just before the pass to the Ossario del Pasubio on the Colle Bellavista.

monte-zugna.intro: A detour on the edge of Rovereto up Monte Zugna, a front-line mountain between Italy and Austria-Hungary in the First World War. A long, quiet hairpin road to over 1,600 m.

sides.character: From Albaredo evenly steep in a long run of hairpins, through forest and higher up across open slopes looking into the Adige valley.
sides.highlights: First World War trenches and positions at the top.

passo-xomo.intro: The little neighbour of the Fugazze above Valli del Pasubio, short and steep. From here the Strada degli Scarubbi continues as a gravel track towards the Pasubio.

sides.character: From Sant'Antonio up in steps and hairpins, with flatter sections between the ramps. Downhill the clearer side.
From Posina quiet and short, steeper and steeper towards the top. The climb with bite, better ridden up.

monte-velo.intro: From Arco up to the alpine pastures above the Sarca valley, where the tarmac ends at the meadows of Monte Velo. Lake Garda lies far below to the south, the climbers' rock faces opposite.

sides.character: From Arco up the slope in many hairpins, growing steeper towards the top. The view over the Sarca valley widens with each bend.
sides.highlights: The view of Arco with its castle and Lake Garda.

valvestino.intro: From Lake Garda at Gargnano into the mountains behind it: first up in hairpins, then through tunnels and galleries high above the fjord-like Valvestino reservoir to Magasa. Almost car-free and one of the finest roads on the western shore.

sides.character: Inland from Gargnano: steeply up in hairpins above the lake, then in steps with counter-climbs along the reservoir, and finally up to the mountain village of Magasa.
sides.highlights: The view down onto the green reservoir.

passo-sommo.intro: The way out of the Adige valley onto the Folgaria plateau: the real work is the hairpin road up from Calliano, the pass beyond it is little more than a rise. Almost 1,200 metres straight above the valley, a serious climb without a big name.

sides.character: From Calliano up the valley side in hairpins, looking back into the Adige valley; a real climb as far as Folgaria, then rolling with short respites to the top.
sides.highlights: The view back into the Adige valley from the hairpins below Folgaria.

passo-delle-fittanze.intro: From Ala in the Adige valley onto the crest of the Lessinia: a good 1,200 metres in one go, with long ramps around 10 % and hardly any traffic. At the top the landscape turns to karst and pasture; on the other side there is only the plateau.

sides.character: Out of the valley via Sega di Ala in many hairpins, the rhythm uneven: long steep ramps alternate with short easier stretches. Pasture and karst open up at the top.
sides.highlights: At the top the open karst country of the Lessinia after the long climb.

passo-di-campogrosso.intro: A steep, shady climb from Recoaro Terme to beneath the rock walls of the Little Dolomites, with a rifugio at the top. Only this side is tarmac, so you ride up here and back down the same way.

sides.character: From Recoaro up the slope in close hairpins, moderate lower down, steeper towards the top. Plenty of forest and shade, and at the end the walls of the Little Dolomites stand right above the road.
sides.highlights: The rock walls of the Little Dolomites above the summit, and the rifugio for a break.

col-de-la-madeleine-bedoin.intro: A small saddle between Malaucène and Bédoin that closes the loop round Mont Ventoux. Hardly a climb, but with an open view of the Ventoux and the jagged Dentelles de Montmirail; it shares only its name with the great Madeleine in Savoie.

sides.character: From Malaucène gently through vineyards and pines, with short flat stretches; a warm-up rather than an effort.
sides.highlights: The Ventoux on your left, the Dentelles de Montmirail to the west.

sides.character: From Bédoin flat and slightly rolling, without hairpins; in either direction a link you ride almost without changing gear.
sides.highlights: Bédoin, the Ventoux start town with its cafés, at the foot.

col-de-notre-dame-des-abeilles.intro: The forest road over the southern flank of the Ventoux from Bédoin to Sault, even and without big hairpin sequences. Besides the Gorges de la Nesque the second way onto the lavender plateau of Sault, quieter and more wooded.

sides.character: From Flassan at an even gradient through oak and pine forest, with a few easier sections; the real climb of the two, a calm ride.
From Sault across the plateau more a rolling rise with a short dip than a climb; in this direction you earn the long, even descent to Flassan.
sides.highlights: Lavender fields around Sault behind you.

col-de-murs.intro: Over the Monts de Vaucluse from the Ventoux country into the Luberon: limestone, oaks and lavender, with hardly any traffic. The village of Murs lies on the way, and beyond it the road drops to Gordes.

sides.character: From Venasque gently at first, then gradually steeper through oak woods and limestone, with a few hairpins higher up; the longer and finer ascent.
sides.highlights: Venasque, one of the villages above the Comtat, at the start.

sides.character: From the village of Murs only a short, moderate rise; as a descent the quiet side towards Gordes and the Luberon.

col-de-perty.intro: One of the highest passes in the Baronnies, ridden by the Tour de France in 2006. From the forest of the Ouvèze the road climbs into a wide bowl, with the Ventoux and the Montagne de Lure on the horizon at the top.

sides.character: From Saint-Auban long and leisurely, with hairpins and easier stretches, out of the forest into the open bowl; as a descent wide and flowing.
sides.highlights: The open bowl below the summit with the view to the Ventoux.

sides.character: From Laborel shorter and steeper, increasingly so towards the top, with a few hairpins; the side that suits climbing.

col-de-soubeyrand.intro: A quiet crossing in the Baronnies between Sainte-Jalle and the Eygues valley. Hairpins through oaks and lavender, and usually you have the road to yourself.

sides.character: From Sainte-Jalle steadily around 6 % in hairpins through oaks and lavender; a climb with a fixed rhythm, ideal for riding up.
sides.highlights: Lavender fields in the hairpins above Sainte-Jalle.

sides.character: From Curnier in the Eygues valley longer and gentler, with calm stretches on the way; as a descent long and relaxed.

col-d-ey.intro: The home climb of Buis-les-Baronnies and the opener of almost every loop there. Short and friendly between olive groves and apricot orchards, with a view of the Ventoux at the top.

sides.character: From Buis up between olives and apricots, gentle below, a little steeper at the top with a few hairpins; the classic way into the loop.
sides.highlights: The view of the Ventoux from the top.

sides.character: From Sainte-Jalle short and almost straight, steeper towards the top; as a descent northwards a short, open stretch.

col-de-fontaube.intro: From Buis via Eygaliers onto a ridge and down into the Toulourenc valley, right beneath the north face of the Ventoux. A small pass with almost no traffic, linking the Baronnies with Brantes and Montbrun.

sides.character: From Eygaliers moderately up in a few hairpins, with easier sections; the real climb of the pass.
From the Toulourenc valley at Brantes hardly a climb; in the other direction the descent with the north face of the Ventoux ahead.
sides.highlights: The north face of the Ventoux above the Toulourenc valley.

col-de-macuegne.intro: A quiet pass between Montbrun-les-Bains and Séderon, over lavender fields and through beech forest. On the Perty loop it is the way back, with the Ventoux in view.

sides.character: From Montbrun steadily over lavender fields into the beech forest, with the Ventoux at your back; in the other direction a calm descent towards the mountain.
sides.highlights: Montbrun-les-Bains, built against the slope, with the Ventoux behind it.

sides.character: From Séderon shorter, a little steeper towards the top, with a few hairpins through forest; the direction of the Perty loop.

col-de-l-homme-mort.intro: The crossing from Montbrun-les-Bains onto the lavender plateau of Ferrassières and Sault. From the west it is hardly a climb, but from Montbrun it is a quiet forest road with a view of the Montagne de Lure.

sides.character: From Montbrun long and mostly moderate through forest, with easier stretches and one short steeper pitch; the plateau opens out at the top.
sides.highlights: The view of the Montagne de Lure, and at the top the lavender fields of the plateau.

col-de-castillon.intro: The direct way from Menton on the sea to Sospel in the Bévéra valley. Through the Careï gorge and past the rebuilt village of Castillon, a pass that takes you from the beach into the mountains in a few kilometres.

sides.character: From Menton at sea level through the Careï gorge, in steps with many hairpins; the lower part has traffic, it gets quieter higher up.
sides.highlights: The village of Castillon just below the top, with a view back to the sea.

sides.character: From Sospel short and steady, with a few hairpins; in this direction a manageable descent into the Bévéra valley.
sides.highlights: Sospel with its old bridge over the Bévéra.

col-d-eze.intro: For decades the closing act of Paris–Nice, as a mountain time trial up from Nice. The Grande Corniche leads to the col with the sea below, and La Turbie and Monaco lie beyond.

sides.character: Out of Nice onto the Grande Corniche, uneven with steeper ramps and easier stretches, hardly any hairpins; the sea below you all the way, and plenty of traffic.
sides.highlights: The view over the Baie des Anges and Nice from the Corniche.

col-saint-roch.intro: The link between the hill villages of Lucéram and Coaraze in the hinterland of Nice. Quiet and twisting, and the piece that turns the Braus and the Turini into a loop.

sides.character: From Lucéram steadily up through a dense run of hairpins; a hairpin wall you can see from below and ride well in rhythm.
sides.highlights: Lucéram, the village on its rocky spur, at the foot.

sides.character: From Coaraze long and stepped, with a drop on the way; laborious as a climb, in the other direction a long descent with the village of Coaraze ahead.
sides.highlights: The hill village of Coaraze on its knoll.

col-de-bleine.intro: The highest crossing between the Estéron and the Thorenc plateau. Beech forest and hairpins lower down, meadows and limestone ridges at the top, high above the Riviera.

sides.character: From Saint-Auban in hairpins through beech forest, stepped with easier stretches and a short dip on the way; meadows and limestone at the top.
sides.highlights: The beech forest in the hairpins of the north side.

sides.character: From the Thorenc plateau only a gentle, rolling rise without hairpins; the better descent, open and quiet.
sides.highlights: A wide view over meadows and limestone ridges at the top.

col-de-l-orme.intro: Really only the first step from Lucéram up to Peïra-Cava and the Col de Turini. Hardly worth mentioning as a pass, but the road on which the loops from Nice over the Turini begin.

sides.character: From Lucéram steadily up the slope in many hairpins, a short, solid climb that carries straight on towards Peïra-Cava.
sides.highlights: The view back down to Lucéram from the hairpins.

col-de-nice.intro: A short hill between the two Paillon valleys of L'Escarène and Contes. Not a goal on its own, but with the Braus and the Saint-Roch a link in the loops behind Nice.

sides.character: From L'Escarène only a short, steady stretch with two hairpins; done in a few minutes.

col-de-la-porte.intro: A quiet crossing above Coaraze over to Lucéram, a little higher than the neighbouring Col Saint-Roch. Hardly any traffic, and on the way the view over the villages of the Paillon valleys.

sides.character: From Coaraze long and stepped, with hairpins, easier stretches and a dip on the way; you gain more height than the average suggests.
sides.highlights: The view over the villages of the Paillon.

col-de-chateauneuf.intro: The first mountain behind Nice towards Tourrette-Levens and Contes, and the opener of many training loops out of the city. Not lonely, but reached within an hour from the sea.

sides.character: From Saint-André-de-la-Roche long and stepped up from the edge of the city, almost without hairpins and with traffic; as a descent wide and quick back to Nice.
From Contes up the slope in a dense run of hairpins, stepped with one steeper pitch; the side to climb.

col-de-brouis.intro: The crossing from Sospel into the Roya valley at Breil, linking Sospel with Tende and the railway line. An honest mid-height pass between olive slopes and forest, easy to combine with the Castillon and the Braus.

sides.character: From Sospel in many hairpins with a changing gradient, easier and steeper stretches in turn; as a descent twisty but not steep.
From Breil steadily and noticeably steeper out of the Roya valley, with more climbing over a shorter distance; the side to climb.
sides.highlights: Breil-sur-Roya on the river, with the view back into the Roya valley.

grand-ballon.intro: The highest point of the Vosges that a road reaches, and on the Tour de France route several times. At the top a wide view over the Rhine plain and the Black Forest, on a clear day as far as the Alps; the summit with its radar dome is a few minutes on foot.

sides.character: From Willer-sur-Thur long in the forest, steadily steeper towards the top, with hairpins in the last third; at the end you leave the trees for the bare dome.
sides.highlights: Leaving the forest for the open dome and its all-round view.

sides.character: From Uffholtz the long side, stepped with easier stretches and a dip, past the Hartmannswillerkopf and then along the crest road; as a descent long and varied.
sides.highlights: The First World War memorial at the Hartmannswillerkopf (Vieil Armand).

ballon-d-alsace.intro: In 1905 the first mountain the Tour de France ever climbed, and many times since. Wide roads from three sides; at the top pastures, inns and a statue of Joan of Arc where Alsace, Lorraine and Franche-Comté meet.

sides.character: From Saint-Maurice-sur-Moselle the shortest and steepest side, steadily around 7 % with hairpins through forest; a climb with a fixed rhythm.
From Giromagny long and gentle, with breathers on the way and wide bends; as a descent flowing and open.
From Sewen up the Doller valley at a changing gradient, easy and steeper stretches in turn, past a reservoir.
sides.highlights: The Lac d'Alfeld just above Sewen.

col-de-la-schlucht.intro: The main crossing from Colmar to Gérardmer, and on the Tour de France route in 2023. The Route des Crêtes starts at the top; the traffic, though, comes with it.

sides.character: From Munster long and steady up the valley, with hairpins and rock above the road near the top; the finer and steeper side.
sides.highlights: The view back into the Munster valley from the upper hairpins.

sides.character: From Gérardmer via Xonrupt almost flat, with short steps; more a roll over than a climb, so the side for the descent.
sides.highlights: The lake at Gérardmer at the foot.

col-du-petit-ballon.intro: A bare dome with mountain inns and a view over the Munster valley and the Rhine plain, ridden on the penultimate stage of the 2023 Tour de France. Narrow, steep and quiet, the opposite of the wide roads of the big Ballons.

sides.character: From Wasserbourg steep and narrow into the forest straight away, a little easier and open over pasture towards the dome.
sides.highlights: A stop at one of the farm inns (fermes-auberges) with the view over the Munster valley.

col-du-platzerwasel.intro: A short, hard climb from the upper Munster valley onto the crest of the Vosges, in 2023 the last climb before the Tour's stage finish at the Markstein. From the south the pass lies at crest height and is no climb of its own.

sides.character: From Sondernach steep and uneven, steep ramps with few real breaks, hairpins in the forest; pastures open up on the crest at the top.
sides.highlights: At the top the crest pastures with a view into the Munster valley.

col-d-oderen.intro: A gentle, wooded crossing from the upper Thur valley to Ventron in the Moselotte valley. No highlight on its own, but a quiet link between Alsace and Lorraine.

sides.character: From Fellering the longer side, moderate and stepped with easier stretches through forest; as a descent long and unproblematic.
From Ventron short, a little steeper towards the top, through forest; a compact climb.

col-de-bussang.intro: The N66 between Thann and Remiremont, flat enough to link rides and with heavy traffic and lorries. Not a goal, just a passage; the Moselle rises at the top.

sides.character: From Saint-Maurice-sur-Moselle flat and straight on the main road, without hairpins; quickly done, but with lorries beside you.
sides.highlights: The source of the Moselle at the top.

sides.character: From Urbès steadily in a few hairpins, more height than from the west; here too on the busy main road.

col-du-bonhomme.intro: The crossing from Kaysersberg to Saint-Dié on the main road, with the traffic to match. Interesting mainly as the gateway to the crest road that branches south at the top towards the Col du Calvaire and the Schlucht.

sides.character: From Lapoutroie the longer side, steepest low down, easing towards the top; as a descent even and with wide bends.
From Plainfaing short and steeper and steeper towards the top, almost without hairpins; straight ramps that are better climbed than descended.

col-du-calvaire.intro: The pass above the Lac Blanc at the northern end of the Vosges crest road. Northwards the road stays at crest height to the Col du Bonhomme; the real climb comes from Orbey.

sides.character: From Orbey steadily and almost without hairpins up through forest, at the end above the Lac Blanc; a climb with an even rhythm.
sides.highlights: The view down to the Lac Blanc beneath its rock wall.

col-de-bramont.intro: A quiet crossing from La Bresse into the uppermost Thur valley at Wildenstein, short and steady. No big name, but a pleasant building block for loops between the Thur and the Moselotte.

sides.character: From Wildenstein steadily up through forest in a run of hairpins; you see them coming and ride them in rhythm.
sides.highlights: The Kruth-Wildenstein reservoir at the foot.

sides.character: From La Bresse gentle and only a little steeper at the top, hardly any hairpins; as a descent the more flowing side.

col-de-grosse-pierre.intro: A short wooded crossing between Gérardmer and the Moselotte valley at Cornimont. Unassuming, but with a steep pitch on the north side that is not to be underestimated.

sides.character: From Gérardmer short and stepped, without hairpins, with one steep ramp between easier stretches and a short dip; the more interesting side to climb.
From Cornimont longer and gentler through forest, with short ramps; the calmer side to descend.

col-du-wettstein.intro: A small pass between the Munster valley and Orbey, marked by the First World War: a military cemetery at the top and the Lingekopf battlefield next to it. Quiet and little used.

sides.character: From Soultzeren steadily around 6 % with a few hairpins through forest; a climb with a fixed rhythm.
sides.highlights: The military cemetery at the top.

sides.character: From Orbey longer and gentler, steady and almost without hairpins; the more relaxed side to descend.
sides.highlights: A detour to the Lingekopf battlefield.

col-de-sainte-marie.intro: The old crossing from Sainte-Marie-aux-Mines into Lorraine. Since most through traffic now takes the Maurice-Lemaire tunnel below it, the pass road has become much quieter.

sides.character: From Sainte-Marie-aux-Mines steeper and steeper towards the top, hardly any hairpins, through forest; the longer climb with the stronger finish.
From Wisembach short and noticeably steep, more so towards the top; a compact climb without hairpins.

col-du-hundsruck.intro: A short wooded pass between Thann and the Doller valley at Masevaux. Useful as an approach to the Ballon d'Alsace, quiet and without much of a view.

sides.character: From Thann uneven and solid, steeper ramps alternating with easier stretches, hardly any hairpins; the harder side.
From Masevaux gentler and stepped, with hairpins and a short dip on the way; the more even side to descend.

hohneck.intro: A spur road from the Route des Crêtes to just below one of the highest summits of the Vosges. At the top a view over the crest, the cirque lakes and on clear days far into the Rhine plain.

sides.character: From La Bresse long and stepped through forest onto the crest, with hairpins and easier sections, at the end over open pasture to the summit area.
sides.highlights: The all-round view from the Hohneck over the crest and the lakes.

la-planche-des-belles-filles.intro: A Tour de France finish since 2012, and in 2020 the scene of the time trial with which Pogačar won the Tour. A short, hard climb in the forest that gets steeper and steeper towards the top.

sides.character: From Plancher-les-Mines moderate at first, then steeper and steeper in the forest up to the ski station; the hardest metres come at the end.
sides.highlights: The Tour's finishing straight at the ski station.

route-des-cretes.intro: The crest road of the high Vosges, built as a supply road in the First World War. It runs over grassy domes with views of the Rhine plain and, on a clear day, the Alps; the Tour de France rides stretches of it too, such as from the Markstein to the Grand Ballon.

sides.character: From the Col de la Schlucht south over the Hohneck and the Markstein to the Grand Ballon: rolling with short climbs and descents, almost always open at crest height.
sides.highlights: The view over the Rhine plain, on clear days as far as the Alps.

gailbergsattel.intro: A wooded saddle below 1,000 m between the Drau and the Gail that links more than it demands. Anyone riding around the Lienz Dolomites or heading for the Plöckenpass passes this way.

sides.character: From Oberdrauburg straight into the hairpins, even and never really steep up through the forest. The side with the rhythm for the climb.
sides.highlights: The view back over the Drau valley.

sides.character: From Kötschach-Mauthen flatter, with one short steep pitch and an almost level stretch before the top. Runs down into the Gail valley without surprises.
sides.highlights: The Gail valley below, with the Carnic Alps.

kartitscher-sattel.intro: An open meadow saddle between the Lienz Dolomites and the Carnic ridge, where the Gail flows east and the Gailbach west. It links the Pustertal with the Lesachtal and is part of the loop around the Lienz Dolomites.

sides.character: From Tassenbach with the steeper ramps and the hairpins up to Kartitsch, then flatter across the meadows to the saddle. The side that asks something of the climb.
sides.highlights: The village of Kartitsch below the Carnic ridge.

sides.character: From Untertilliach gentle and long beside the young Gail through Obertilliach, with short rollers in between. Downhill a long roll through the upper Lesachtal.
sides.highlights: Obertilliach and its compact village centre.

passo-cimabanche.intro: Hardly a climb, more a long valley between the Pustertal and the Ampezzo, but one with a Dolomite backdrop. Usually ridden as the approach to the Drei Zinnen, Misurina or Cortina, with the old Dolomite railway as a cycle path alongside.

sides.character: From Toblach long and barely rising through the Höhlensteintal, past two lakes and with short flat stretches. Uphill, Monte Cristallo grows ahead of you.
sides.highlights: The Dürrensee with Monte Cristallo behind it.

sides.character: From Cortina just as gentle up through the forest along the Boite, with a bare plateau at the top. Downhill fast and open into the Cortina basin.
