sides.highlights: The Tofane above the Ampezzo.

passo-sant-antonio.intro: A quiet forest pass between the Ansiei valley at Auronzo and the Comelico, also called Passo del Zovo. Short, but steep throughout on the south side, and with Monte Croce Comelico a loop around the Comelico.

sides.character: Flat out of Auronzo, then steep in the middle section with hairpins through the forest; the view opens near the top. A side for climbing, uncomfortable downhill because of the ramps.
sides.highlights: At the top, the view across the forests of the Comelico.

sides.character: From Padola short with a few steep pitches, on a wide road with a good surface. Downhill the pleasanter side into the Comelico.
sides.highlights: Padola below the meadows of the Comelico.

reschenpass.intro: The old Via Claudia Augusta crossing from the Inn to the Adige, today a wide transit road. It is known above all for the church tower of old Graun rising out of the Reschensee, and for the open Malser Haide with the Ortler behind.

sides.character: From Mals the only noticeable climb is across the Malser Haide up to the Haidersee, then almost level along the two lakes. Often into a headwind and with heavy traffic; a cycle path runs alongside.
sides.highlights: The church tower in the Reschensee at Graun.

norbertshoehe.intro: A hairpin road from the Lower Engadine up to the Nauders plateau which, with the Finstermünz gorge closed to bikes, has become the real cycle route to the Reschenpass. The Via Claudia Augusta runs on it too.

sides.character: From Martina straight into a series of hairpins on the slope above the Inn, even and without hard ramps to the top. Rides well, but with buses and diverted traffic.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Lower Engadine and the Inn gorge.

passo-croce-d-aune.intro: A low forest pass above Feltre that owes its fame to a story: this is where Tullio Campagnolo is said to have had the idea for the quick release. Today a quiet climb with a small village, hotels and inns at the top.

sides.character: From Pedavena steep and even at once in hairpins through the forest, with no flat stretches to the saddle. The side for climbing.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Campagnolo monument on the saddle.

sides.character: From Gorna more varied through the hamlets of Sovramonte, with flatter stretches and short dips between the hairpins. Downhill the finer side, with views over the valley.
sides.highlights: The villages of Sovramonte on the slope.

colle-d-esischie.intro: A saddle between the Rocce Ciarmetta and Monte Pelvo where the road from the Vallone di Marmora meets the Fauniera road. Most riders carry on to the Colle Fauniera; the Granfondo Fausto Coppi climbs up from the Maira valley this way.

sides.character: From Ponte Marmora irregular, with a few very short ramps around 19 % and two kilometres around 10 % low down, then calmer at 6–8 % over the pastures. Long, lonely and narrow.
sides.highlights: The view back over the Marmora basin from the top.

madonna-del-colletto.intro: A low crossing over the ridge between the Valle Stura and the Valle Gesso, with the Santuario Madonna del Colletto at the top. Known as the final climb of the Granfondo Fausto Coppi, which rides up from Festiona and down to Valdieri.

sides.character: From Festiona through forest, with several ramps above 12 % in the first half, then steadier. Old, uneven tarmac with grit, the better choice uphill.
sides.highlights: The little church on the saddle.

sides.character: From Valdieri shorter and steep throughout, in hairpins above the Gesso valley, with a stretch of concrete near the top. The Granfondo descends this way.
sides.highlights: The view over the Gesso valley out towards Cuneo.

forcella-aurine.intro: A quiet saddle at the foot of the Pale di San Martino, crossed by the SP347 from Agordo to Gosaldo and on to the Passo Cereda. With the Forcella Franche it makes the loop around the Gosaldo valley.

sides.character: From the Cordevole bridge near Agordo straight up at around 7 % in hairpins to Voltago, then steadily on via Frassenè; it eases near the top. A climb that is easy to pace.
sides.highlights: Frassenè beneath the walls of the Agnèr.

forcella-franche.intro: A low saddle between the Agordo basin and the wild Valle del Mis. On the south side the road runs through a narrow gorge with a reservoir and short, dark tunnels, one of the quietest corners of the Belluno Dolomites.

sides.character: From Ponte Alto near Agordo on a wide road via Rivamonte, moderately steep with a few short, harder pitches. Downhill a flowing roll-out.
sides.highlights: The view from Rivamonte over the Agordo basin.

sides.character: From Titele, where the road leaves the Mis gorge, clearly steeper in hairpins up via Tiser, narrow and with ramps up to 12 %. Coming up the valley you first ride through the unlit tunnels along the Lago del Mis.
sides.highlights: The village of Tiser and the view down into the Mis gorge.

col-de-la-bataille.intro: A Vercors pass whose top lies just past a short tunnel through the rock, after which the view opens over the Combe de Bouvante. With the Combe Laval and the Col de la Machine it makes one of the finest loops in the Vercors.

sides.character: From Léoncel through forest, with a long stretch just under 9 % in the first half, the last two kilometres almost flat. The tunnel just before the col is windy.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Combe de Bouvante after the tunnel.

brennerpass.intro: The busiest crossing of the Alps, but for cyclists it is the old main road away from the motorway. Not a mountain that asks much, rather the link between Innsbruck and South Tyrol that the Ötztaler rides between the Kühtai and the Jaufen.

sides.character: Out of Innsbruck first the steeper ramp up to Schönberg, then a long, almost level run up the Wipptal through Matrei and Steinach; just before the top it kicks up once more. You gain height without noticing, a rolling road in either direction.
sides.highlights: The Brennersee just below the top.

sides.character: From Sterzing flat out of town at first, the steeper stretch at Gossensass, then easy again up the upper Eisack valley. Shorter than the north side and with what little climbing the Brenner has.
sides.highlights: Gossensass at the mouth of the Pflersch valley.

col-des-gets.intro: A low saddle between the Chablais and the Giffre with the ski resort of Les Gets on top. More of a passage than a goal: the Route des Grandes Alpes between Morzine and Cluses, and the way to the Joux Plane and the Ramaz.

sides.character: From Taninges gentle and even up to the turn-off for the Col de la Ramaz, then about 2 km a little steeper, flattening again before Les Gets. One stretch runs through a shady, cool gorge.
sides.highlights: The view down over the Giffre valley.

sides.character: From Morzine short and moderate on a wide road, more a link between two ski resorts than a climb. Over quickly in either direction.
sides.highlights: Les Gets itself, with the Mont Chéry above the top.

passo-pampeago.intro: The Reiterjoch below the Latemar links the Val di Fiemme with the Eggental and is known above all as the Giro summit finish at the Alpe di Pampeago. For the 2012 Giro the last stretch to the pass was paved, and since then it is a through road that stays closed to cars.

sides.character: From Tesero steep at once and hardly easing up through the forest to the ski station, then steeper again on the car-free stretch to the pass. Hard and even; downhill it is the wider road.
sides.highlights: On the way, the memorial to the Stava disaster of 1985.

sides.character: From Birchabruck with very steep ramps up to Obereggen, then single-track and quieter through forest and across pastures to the pass. Uncomfortable downhill because of the ramps and the narrow road.
sides.highlights: The Latemar above the pastures near Obereggen.
